html:
In October 2008 Iceland's three main banks collapsed within a week. Relative to the size of its economy, it was one of the largest banking failures in history.

After the banks were privatised around 2003 they borrowed heavily abroad and grew to many times the size of the economy, taking deposits from savers in Britain and the Netherlands through internet accounts such as Icesave. When credit dried up in the world financial crisis, they could not pay. The krona crashed, and Britain used an anti-terror law to freeze Icelandic assets.

Protests banging pots and pans brought down the government. Iceland let the banks fail rather than saving their foreign creditors, and voters twice rejected deals to repay Icesave. Several bankers were jailed. The economy recovered within a few years, helped by tourism after the eruption of 2010. See Iceland.
sum: In October 2008 Iceland's three main banks collapsed within a week. Relative to the size of its economy, it was one of the largest banking failures in history.
